key_insight: FedLG integrates a Lanczos-based projection into a federated graph learning pipeline to align and aggregate heterogeneous molecular graph representations across parties, enabling collaborative molecular discovery without sharing raw data. The approach yields robust, improved performance across diverse molecular tasks.
problem_solved: Enables multi-party collaboration for molecular discovery while preserving data privacy and handling heterogeneity in graph structures and feature distributions that typically degrade federated model performance.
method: Federated graph learning: train local GNNs on private molecular graphs and share only compressed representations or model updates.
Lanczos-based projection: project high-dimensional local graph embeddings into a low-dimensional, aligned subspace to enable efficient, robust aggregation across heterogeneous parties.
Global aggregation and optional fine-tuning: aggregate projected representations centrally (or via secure protocols) and fine-tune global models for downstream molecular tasks.
impact: Permits chemistry and drug-discovery teams to collaboratively train GNNs without centralizing sensitive molecular datasets, improving generalization across datasets and reducing communication/heterogeneity bottlenecks for real-world federated deployments.
